name: Vedaranyeswarar Temple, Vedaranyam
deity: Shiva as Vedaranyeswarar, lord of the forest of the Vedas, with the Thyagaraja processional deity Bhuvani Vidangar and the Goddess Vedanayaki
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram; the stone temple of the Chola age
summary: At Vedaranyam, near the southern mouth of the Kaveri by the sea, Shiva stands as Vedaranyeswarar, the lord of the forest of the Vedas; the Thyagaraja of the shrine — Bhuvani Vidangar — is the last of the seven dancing Thyagarajas of the delta, whose procession is said to move in the Hamsapada Natanam.

sections.history: Vedaranyam — the forest of the Vedas — lies near the sea at the southern edge of the Kaveri delta, where the coast turns toward Point Calimere. Its temple to Shiva as Vedaranyeswarar, with the Goddess Vedanayaki, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of great antiquity, sung by the Nayanmar saints, its stone shrines of the Chola age. It is one of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams, and its Thyagaraja is honoured as Bhuvani Vidangar, held to be the last of the seven Vidangas of the dancing tradition.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner, the temple gathers around the sanctum of Vedaranyeswarar, with the Goddess Vedanayaki in her own shrine and the Somaskanda Thyagaraja — Shiva with Uma and the child Skanda — worshipped as the uncarved Vidanga and carried as the processional lord. Tall gopurams and pillared halls open before the sanctum, in the manner of the great delta temples of the Chola and later ages.
sections.legends: The name Vedaranyam recalls the legend that the four Vedas themselves worshipped Shiva here in the form of a forest, and that the temple's doors are opened and closed by their grace; the child-saint Sambandar is remembered for the hymn that opened them. As one of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams, its Thyagaraja is Bhuvani Vidangar, whose procession is said to move in the Hamsapada Natanam, the dance likened to the gait of a swan.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the festivals of Shiva and of Thyagaraja through the year, with the procession of the Vidangar and the days of the Nayanmar saints at the heart of its celebration, and the coastal Aadi and Masi observances drawing the surrounding country.
sections.experience: Vedaranyam rewards the pilgrim who reaches the sea-edge of the delta with a great Shaiva temple and the last of the seven dancing Thyagarajas, near the wide salt flats and the bird sanctuary of Point Calimere. It closes the pilgrimage of the seven Vidanga shrines that begins inland at Thiruvarur.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days and processions are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Vedaranyam lies near the coast at the southern edge of the Kaveri delta, about 55 km from Nagapattinam, well connected by road; it is the gateway to Point Calimere.
